label: late original-phase / <DEL> steps, boosted when sequence starts with s/w/v/c
explanation: Fires only at steps t=4..9 of the original phase and at the <DEL> step (78% / 22% of mass); never in the copy phase or at t<4. Positional gating alone has ~92% recall but only 7% precision. Within that window, firing is much more likely when the first original token is s, w, v or c (4-4.5x lift), and when the current input is h (4.9x lift; top activations are almost all h at t=7-8 followed by <DEL>). Longer sequences (L=8,9) and first occurrences of the input token fire more. Predicate (late steps & first token in s/w/v/c) gets dev F1 0.35, mass recall 0.54; adding in_tok==h raises F1 to 0.38. The remaining dependence looks like a distributed function of the earlier tokens that no simple predicate captures.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: s, w, v, c, j, e; least: x, 2, 1, h) and the current input token, by step (t=7: h, l, 2, i; t=8: h, l, 2, i; t=6: h, i, l, 2); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=7, L=9 & t=8.
